title: Shared audit logging library + schema validator; lint unregistered audit event names
creator: Nadia Rahman
description:
Context
We’re standardizing audit logs across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private. ENG-2481 defines the canonical audit event schema v1, but we need enforcement so services can’t emit malformed events or invent event names ad-hoc.

This issue implements:
1) A shared audit logging library used by services to emit and validate audit events against schema v1.
2) A registry of allowed event names (and versions) and a lint/build-time check to block unregistered event names.

Goals / outcomes
- Make it the "easy path" for services to emit compliant audit events.
- Catch schema violations early (unit tests / build-time / CI) before events reach the pipeline.
- Prevent taxonomy drift: no new audit event name without registering it and documenting it.

Non-goals
- Implement instrumentation for specific sensitive actions (tracked in ENG-2483+ and service tickets).
- Add sampling (explicitly not allowed for audit logs).

Proposed approach
A) Schema + types
- Store JSONSchema for audit event schema v1 in-repo (canonical source).
- Provide typed helpers for common fields and safe construction:
  - event_name, schema_version
  - actor (type, id, org/workspace where relevant)
  - target (type, id, display where relevant)
  - request_id / trace_id
  - ip, user_agent (with explicit guidance on when to include; allow null)
  - outcome (success/failure), error_code (stable), error_message (redacted), http_status
  - timestamp (server-side)
- Provide a validator that can run:
  - in-service (fast, deterministic, no network)
  - in pipeline (authoritative validation + DLQ)

B) Registry + lint rule
- Introduce an audit-event registry file (source of truth for allowed names) with:
  - event_name
  - schema_version(s) supported
  - owning team/service (for inventory + routing of questions)
  - stability level (experimental/internal/ga) if needed later
- Add build-time check that fails CI when:
  - code references an event name not present in registry
  - registry entries violate naming conventions (naming guidelines doc)
- Implementation detail: keep the lint lightweight so it doesn’t require full AST parsing for all languages. Prefer a simple pattern:
  - services call a helper emitAuditEvent({ eventName: AuditEventName.X }) where AuditEventName is generated from registry
  - codegen step generates language-specific enum/constants from registry

C) Backward compatibility
- Allow dual-write in instrumentation tickets (old event name + new schema-v1 name) via config, but registry must include both names during migration windows.

Acceptance criteria
- [x] JSONSchema for audit event schema v1 merged and versioned
- [x] Shared helper types + validate(event) available for services
- [x] Registry exists and is reviewed/owned (Security Eng + Telemetry)
- [x] CI fails if an unregistered event name is referenced (at minimum in the main redwood monorepo)
- [x] Developer docs in-repo: how to add a new audit event name (registry update + review) and how to emit + test
- [x] Unit tests for validator + registry checks

Implementation notes
- Performance: validator should be fast; we should not validate multiple times per request unnecessarily. Recommended pattern: validate at emission boundary (where event object is created) and rely on pipeline validation as backstop.
- Redaction: library should include safe error serialization helpers so we don’t leak tokens/secrets in error_message or payload.
- Strictness: schema validation errors should be treated as production bugs. In prod, emission should:
  - emit a metric + log error
  - optionally fall back to emitting a minimal "audit.validation_failed" event (TBD with Security) OR drop (Security leaning: drop + alert to avoid poisoning logs)

Rollout plan
1) Land schema + validator + registry + lint in monorepo.
2) Update 1–2 early services (API key instrumentation, RBAC) to use the library.
3) Make lint non-blocking for 1 week (warning mode) if needed, then flip to blocking.

Links
- Related: ENG-2481 (schema v1 definition)
- GitHub: PR #18421 (schema v1 + helper types)
- GitHub: PR #18437 (audit-event registry + build-time check)

comments: 2025-05-23 (Nadia Rahman): Creating this as a platform dependency for the rest of the instrumentation tickets. Strong preference from Security: no free-form event names; we need registry + enforcement.

2025-05-24 (Benji Okafor): Proposal: registry as YAML/JSON + codegen of constants to avoid AST parsing. Validator will wrap AJV (TS) for console/backend services; for Go services we can use gojsonschema in a small helper (or validate in pipeline only). Need decision on whether we require in-service validation everywhere or allow pipeline-only for some languages.

2025-05-26 (Marcus Lin): +1 registry + codegen. For validation: pipeline validation is required, but in-service validation is strongly preferred for anything that can emit. If a service can’t validate (language gap), it must at least use generated event-name constants and include required envelope fields.

2025-05-28 (Allison Grant): Please include metric names for validation failures (e.g., auditlog.validation_failed.count by service/event_name) and ensure request_id/trace_id propagation fields are first-class in the helper.
2025-05-30 (Benji Okafor): PR up for schema + helper types: redwood/pr_18421. Includes JSONSchema + unit tests. Next PR will add registry + CI check.

2025-06-03 (Benji Okafor): PR redwood/pr_18437 adds registry + build-time check. CI now fails on unknown event names in the audit logger callsites. Added docs: /docs/internal/audit-logging.md (how to register event, naming rules, and test guidance).

2025-06-04 (Kaitlyn Nguyen): Confirmed API keys service can migrate to emitAuditEvent() helper cleanly. The generated constants are a big win; reduces typo risk. Please ensure registry supports dual-write names during migration.

2025-06-05 (Marcus Lin): Approved with note: default behavior on validation failure should be "do not emit" + alert/metric, not emitting a secondary event (avoid recursive failure modes). Follow-up: ensure redaction helper is used in all error serialization paths.

2025-06-07 (Benji Okafor): Merged #18421 and #18437. CI gate is blocking by default. Follow-ups filed in instrumentation tickets to adopt library across remaining services; validator + registry now treated as required dependency for new sensitive actions.
